;Business and economy
*[[China–United States trade war]]
**[[China|Chinese]] IT company [[ByteDance]] agrees to [[divest]] from the [[United States|U.S.]] branch of [[TikTok]], in light of [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s threat to ban the app within the country. If the deal is approved, [[Microsoft]] will handle the app's personal data rather than ByteDance, averting a main source of contention with U.S. officials. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-tiktok-bytedance-exclusive/exclusive-tiktoks-chinese-owner-offers-to-forego-stake-to-clinch-u-s-deal-sources-idUSKBN24X3SK (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Isaias]]  
***[[Saffir–Simpson scale|Category One]] Isaias makes landfall on northern [[Andros, Bahamas|Andros Island]] heading toward [[Grand Bahama]]. The storm, strength slightly reduced to 75 mph (120 km/h) with heavy rains and coastal flooding, will move over the [[Straits of Florida]] tonight and approach the southeast coast of [[Florida]] early Sunday. [[North Carolina]] orders the evacuation of [[Ocracoke, North Carolina|Ocracoke Island]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/08/01/hurricane-isaias-track-north-carolina-bahamas-florida-saturday/5562047002/ (''USA Today'')] [https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/refresh/MIATCPAT4+shtml/011740.shtml (National Hurricane Center)]
*[[2020 Punjab alcohol poisoning]]
**Officials say at least 86 people have died in recent days due to consuming toxic [[Bootlegging (alcohol)|illegally-made alcohol]] in [[Punjab, India]]. [[Indian Police Service|Police]] are carrying out raids in the state, confiscating supplies of the suspected alcohol and have made 25 arrests. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-india-53624507 (BBC News)]
*[[Flash flood]]s in [[Nangarhar]], [[Afghanistan]], kill 16 people, injure four others and damage several houses. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/16-dead-mostly-children-nangarhar-flash-floods (TOLONews)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] declares a [[state of emergency]] for two weeks until August 15 and asks people to stay home after the popular tourist destination sees an "explosive spread" of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/japans-okinawa-declares-state-of-emergency-as-coronavirus-cases-soar (''The Straits Times'')]
****Tokyo reports 472 new cases, its highest toll to date for the city. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/08/01/national/tokyo-logs-another-record-coronavirus/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]]
****The [[Kuwait]]i Directorate General of Civil Aviation bans flights to 31 countries as [[Kuwait International Airport]] resumes operations at reduced capacity. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-airlines-kuwait/kuwait-bans-flights-to-31-high-risk-countries-due-to-coronavirus-idUSKBN24X3QC?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports a record more than 57,000 new cases, as well as 764 deaths in the last 24 hours. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/over-57-000-coronavirus-cases-in-biggest-1-day-jump-in-india-16-95-lakh-total-cases-so-far-36-511-deaths-2272371 (NDTV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] report 4,963 new cases, its highest toll to date. The cases rise to 98,232 and the deaths jump by 17 to reach a total of 2,039. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-philippines-cases/philippines-confirms-nearly-5000-new-coronavirus-cases-largest-single-day-increase-idUSKBN24X3MT?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Queensland]] closes its border with [[Greater Sydney]] at 1 a.m. ([[Time in Australia|AEST]]) after its premier [[Annastacia Palaszczuk]] declared all of [[Sydney]] a COVID-19 hotspot on July 29. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/queensland-shuts-its-borders-greater-sydney-millions-coronavirus-cases-nsw-clusters/c840a314-1ed3-4daa-a3d8-74e88c82b76b (9 News)]
***Australian COVID-19 death toll reaches 200. [https://www.smh.com.au/national/live-updates-coronavirus-victoria-braces-for-stage-four-lockdown-after-high-covid-19-cases-aged-care-crisis-continues-nsw-battles-clusters-australian-death-toll-jumps-to-201-20200802-p55ho8.html (''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***South Africa surpasses 500,000 cases after adding a total of 10,107 new cases Saturday night. [https://apnews.com/a032151efc882a4f02845b91b9805ca0 (AP)]

;Law and crime
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]], [[Religion in South Korea]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion]]
**[[Lee Man-hee]], a [[Shincheonji Church of Jesus]] [[pastor]], is arrested for allegedly hiding contact information from virus trackers and [[embezzling]] 5.6 billion [[South Korean won|won]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/01/south-korean-sect-leader-arrested-for-obstructing-covid-19-investigation (''The Guardian'')]
*12 people, including [[Booker Prize]]-nominated author [[Tsitsi Dangarembga]], are released from detention by [[Zimbabwe]]an authorities for participating in anti-government protests in the capital of [[Harare]] yesterday. They are to return for trials on September 18. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/zimbabwean-author-tsitsi-dangarembga-released-bail-200801151619032.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Ministry of Intelligence (Iran)|Iranian Ministry of Intelligence]] announces the detainment of Jamshid Sharmahd, the leader of the pro-[[Pahlavi dynasty|Pahlavi]] group [[Kingdom Assembly of Iran]], for coordinating the [[2008 Shiraz explosion|2008 attack on worshippers]] in [[Shiraz]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-usa-security/iran-says-it-has-detained-u-s-based-opposition-leader-over-2008-bomb-attack-idUSKBN24X3TI?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Khabarovsk Krai protests]]
**Protests in the [[Russian Far East|Far Eastern]] city of [[Khabarovsk]], [[Russia]] continue for the fourth consecutive weekend. Protesters demand the release of regional governor [[Sergei Furgal]], who was arrested on charges of murder, which he denies. Thousands of people reportedly join the protest. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-politics-governor/anti-kremlin-protest-in-russias-far-east-attracts-thousands-for-a-fourth-weekend-idUSKBN24X3LG (Reuters)]
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**A demonstration against coronavirus restrictions attended by thousands of people in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]], is terminated by police over "non-respect of hygiene rules". Police say they launched legal action against the organisers. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/thousands-germans-protest-coronavirus-restrictions-200801161142837.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Science and technology
*The [[Barakah nuclear power plant]] in the [[United Arab Emirates]] becomes operational following delays since 2017. It is the first commercial [[nuclear power station]] in the [[Arab world]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-53619916 (BBC News)]
